overview:
**Extreme fire danger holds today across the Montrose High Elevation zone, driven by critically dry fuels (ERC at 97%) and low humidity.**
- Danger eases slightly to Very High Wednesday, then holds at High the rest of the week as humidity partially recovers.
- Afternoon isolated storms are possible today, but with only 0.04" rain and winds shifting NE at 7 mph, they add lightning risk more than relief.
- Watchout status: 3 of 7 local thresholds exceeded (ERC, minimum humidity, 1000-hr fuels) — no active Red Flag Warning is posted for the area right now.
- Stage 2 Fire Restrictions are in effect across all of Montrose County as of August 8, with fire danger rated extreme; Ouray and Delta counties are also under Stage 2, and BLM's Uncompahgre/Gunnison Gorge lands remain under Stage 1.
- Nearby: the Gold Mountain fire two miles north of Ouray, CO, is 39,532 acres and 90% contained; the Elk fire seven miles northwest of Lake City is 7,071 acres, 33% contained, with evacuations still active.
